trusted.author: bestdan
trusted.title: co-review: scope "run the validator" to fixtures in the diff
trusted.body:
`skills/co-review/SKILL.md:513` tells the main agent to execute the real validator when "the diff adds or edits validation fixtures — or the schema/rules that validate them". The rule says nothing about claims outside the diff, and an agent stretches it: when a reviewer disputes a factual claim about how a tool behaved (for example, what a validator accepted in an earlier version), the agent sets up and runs that tool to settle a question the diff does not raise. That spends review time, and against code other than what is under review it can produce a confident answer about the wrong thing.

## Proposed change

- State explicitly that the validator rule applies only to fixtures and schema/rules changed in the diff under review.
- Add the case it does not cover: when a reviewer disputes a factual claim about behavior outside the diff (historical behavior, an unchanged tool), do not run external validation to settle it. Mark the finding unverified and surface it as a judgment call, or skip it with a coverage note.

## Acceptance criteria

- The validator bullet names its scope as "changed in this diff".
- The skill says how to handle a disputed out-of-diff behavioral claim, and that handling does not involve running tools against code outside the diff.
